title: Stormshield
desc: European network security: firewalls, endpoint and data

pages.t: Stormshield makes cyber security products and is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Airbus Defence and Space Cyber Programmes. It positions itself as a European security vendor for sensitive and critical infrastructures.
g: The company that makes a product. Allnet is the distributor in between.
A company owned by a bigger parent company.

pages.t: The products cover network (firewalls), endpoint (protecting PCs and servers) and data (encrypting files). One vendor, three layers, so a customer can protect the whole chain instead of only one door.
g: A device a person or process uses: laptop, PC or server.
A security box between networks that decides which traffic is allowed through.

pages.t: Stormshield lists sectors such as defence, public administration, healthcare, water, electric utilities, transport and aviation. These are customers who care where a product comes from and what it is certified for.

quiz.q: Who owns Stormshield?
o: Airbus Defence and Space Cyber Programmes
quiz.w: Stormshield is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Airbus Defence and Space Cyber Programmes.

quiz.q: Which three areas do Stormshield products cover?
quiz.w: The range is network (firewalls), endpoint (PCs and servers) and data (encryption).

quiz.q: Which kind of customer is a typical Stormshield fit?
o: A small online shop with no security needs
A public body that cares about European origin and certification
quiz.w: Stormshield lists public administration, defence and other sensitive sectors as its markets.
g: Scrambling data so only people with the key can read it.

pages.t: SNS (Stormshield Network Security) is the firewall range for normal IT networks. It combines UTM and next-generation firewall features, so one box handles filtering, intrusion prevention, VPN and web control.
g: Unified Threat Management: many security functions in one box.
Next-generation firewall: understands applications and threats, not just ports.
A secure tunnel over the internet between sites or to a person.

pages.t: Models are named by size. Entry models such as the SN170 and the SN-S series are a usual starting point for small sites. SN-M targets growing businesses, SN1100 multi-site companies, and SN-L and SN-XL larger, high-performance setups.
g: A small branch or shop connected back to head office.
A big firewall that many remote sites connect into.

pages.t: All SNS firewalls run the same firmware. A customer who grows from a small box to a big one keeps the same software base. That should make it easier for resellers to learn once and sell across sizes.
g: The operating software inside a device.

quiz.q: What does SNS stand for in Stormshield's range?
quiz.w: SNS is Stormshield Network Security, the firewall range.

quiz.q: A customer has 30 staff and one small office. Which group is the natural starting point?
quiz.w: The SN-S series is a usual starting point for small businesses. Always check the exact model with Stormshield.
g: Small SNS models, for small offices.

quiz.q: What is the benefit of the single firmware across all SNS models?
quiz.w: All SNS firewalls are based on the same firmware, from small to large boxes.

quiz.q: Which fits an SN-L or SN-XL best?
o: A large head office or busy hub
quiz.w: SN-L and SN-XL are the larger, higher-performance models, so they suit big sites rather than a small kiosk.

lessons.title: SNi and SNxr: when the box goes to a factory

pages.t: SNi firewalls (SNi10, SNi20, SNi40, SNi50) protect OT: factory floors, water plants and power networks. They mount on a DIN rail in a control cabinet and help segment the network to limit attack spread.
g: Operational Technology: machines and control systems that run physical processes.
Standard metal rail inside industrial cabinets.
Splitting a network into zones so a problem cannot spread.

pages.t: Industrial boxes offer high availability and a safety mode so production continues if the firewall fails. They also check industrial messages and protect PLCs. The SNi40 is off sale and Stormshield points customers to the SNi50.
g: Industrial controller that runs a machine.
Two devices so one takes over if the other fails.

pages.t: SNxr1200 is an extra-ruggedized model, designed to be embedded in vehicles operating in critical environments. It is a different job from a factory box: not a cabinet in a plant, but equipment built for harsh field conditions.
g: Built to survive shock, dust, water and extreme temperatures.

quiz.q: What does OT mean?
quiz.w: OT is the machines and control systems that run physical processes.

quiz.q: A water utility wants to protect pumps and PLCs in control cabinets. Which line?
quiz.w: SNi is the industrial range built for operational networks and cabinets.

quiz.q: Which SNi model does Stormshield point to now that the SNi40 is off sale?
quiz.w: The SNi40 page says it is off sale and points to the SNi50.

quiz.q: Which model is built to be embedded in vehicles in critical environments?
quiz.w: The SNxr1200 is the extra-ruggedized model for vehicles in critical environments.

lessons.title: SES: protecting the laptops and servers

pages.t: SES (Stormshield Endpoint Security) is software on workstations and servers. It detects and blocks suspicious behaviour in real time, such as attempts to exploit system flaws. A firewall guards the network, SES guards the machine itself.
g: Using a software flaw to break in.

pages.t: Stormshield says SES works without signatures, meaning it does not need a list of known malware. It also offers ransomware protection and threat hunting. This kind of product is called EDR: detection and response on endpoints.
g: Malware that locks files and demands payment.

pages.t: SES can run on-premises, as SaaS or via a managed service provider. It also holds a first-level CSPN certification from the French agency ANSSI, which matters to sensitive sectors.
g: Software run by the vendor in the cloud.
Managed Security Service Provider: a company that runs security for others.
A French first-level security certification for products.

quiz.q: What does SES protect?
quiz.w: SES is endpoint security for PCs and servers.

quiz.q: What does 'works without signatures' mean?
o: It needs a human to approve each file
It does not rely on a list of known malware
quiz.w: It detects suspicious behaviour instead of matching known malware fingerprints.

quiz.q: A customer already has a firewall but worries about laptops. What is the answer?
quiz.w: The firewall protects the network edge, SES protects each machine.

quiz.q: How can SES be deployed?
o: On-premises, SaaS or via a managed provider
quiz.w: The options are on-premises, SaaS and a managed service through a certified MSSP.

pages.t: SDS (Stormshield Data Security) encrypts sensitive information end to end, so it is not sent or stored in plain text. Even if someone gets the file, they cannot read it without access rights.
g: Data stays encrypted from sender to receiver.

pages.t: Stormshield says the keys stay under the company's control, so even administrators cannot read protected data. Access is set by groups and profiles. That is the pitch for regulated or secretive organisations.
g: The secret that unlocks encrypted data.

pages.t: SDS Enterprise is the core. SDS for Google Workspace adds encryption to Google tools. Smart File Reader is free software for recipients. Data Connector builds it into business apps. An encryption portal shares files with outsiders.
g: Google's online office and mail suite.

quiz.q: What is SDS mainly for?
quiz.w: SDS is the encryption line.

quiz.q: Who holds the encryption keys, according to Stormshield?
quiz.w: The keys stay under the customer's control.

quiz.q: A partner receives encrypted files but will not buy the full product. What fits?
quiz.w: Smart File Reader is the free reader for encrypted packages.

quiz.q: Which customer fits SDS for Google Workspace?
o: One using Google Workspace for mail and docs
quiz.w: It adds encryption to data stored in Google tools.

lessons.title: Managing many firewalls: SMC, SLS and XDR

pages.t: SMC (Stormshield Management Center) is for customers with many sites and many SNS firewalls. It gives one central place to deploy configuration, push updates and watch firewalls and VPN tunnels.
g: A company with several offices, shops or plants.
A secure link between two sites.

pages.t: SLS (Stormshield Log Supervisor) is a SIEM: it collects event logs from firewalls, SES agents and many other sources into one view. It keeps logs for years, useful for audits and compliance.
g: Security Information and Event Management: central log analysis.
A record of what happened on a device.

pages.t: Stormshield XDR combines SNS, SES and threat intelligence, orchestrated by SLS, to correlate events across network and endpoints and send real-time alerts. It is a package idea for customers who run both.
g: Extended Detection and Response: connects alerts from several security layers.

quiz.q: A retailer has 80 shops, each with an SNS firewall. What helps manage them?
quiz.w: SMC is central administration for multi-site SNS deployments.

quiz.q: What does SLS mainly do?
quiz.w: SLS is a SIEM for log management.

quiz.q: What does XDR combine?
quiz.w: XDR links SNS, SES and Stormshield threat intelligence, orchestrated by SLS.

quiz.q: A single small office with one firewall asks about SMC. Likely answer?
o: Not needed, SMC is for many firewalls
quiz.w: SMC targets organisations with several SNS firewalls across sites.

pages.t: EVA (Elastic Virtual Appliance) is Stormshield's virtual firewall. Instead of a box, it runs as software in a data centre or cloud, protecting servers and services that live there.
g: A device delivered as software that runs on a virtual machine.
Software that runs virtual machines, e.g. VMware or Hyper-V.

pages.t: EVA runs on common hypervisors such as VMware, Hyper-V and KVM, and is available in clouds like AWS, Azure, 3DS Outscale and OVHcloud. Its performance scales with the CPU and memory you give it.
g: An app store inside a cloud provider.

pages.t: Pick EVA when the workload is in the cloud or virtualised and a hardware box makes no sense. Stormshield describes it as developed entirely in France, which can appeal to customers who care about trusted, sovereign options.
g: Under local legal control, not subject to foreign rules.

quiz.q: What is EVA?
quiz.w: EVA is the virtual firewall range.

quiz.q: A customer moves servers into Azure. Which Stormshield product?
quiz.w: EVA is built for cloud and virtual environments.

quiz.q: What decides EVA performance?
quiz.w: Performance scales with the vCPU and vRAM allocated.

quiz.q: A factory floor with PLCs needs a firewall in a cabinet. Is EVA right?
o: No, an SNi industrial firewall fits better
quiz.w: EVA is software for virtual or cloud workloads, SNi is the cabinet-mounted industrial option.

pages.t: A certification means an independent body tested the product. Governments and defence buyers often ask for it. Stormshield lists Common Criteria EAL4+ and ANSSI Standard qualification, the French agency's approval level.
g: International standard for testing IT security products.
The French national cyber security agency.

pages.t: Stormshield also shows EU RESTRICTED and NATO RESTRICTED labels. These are classification levels for sensitive but not top-secret information, so buyers handling such data can look at these products.
g: A low classification level for sensitive government information.

pages.h: What to say, and not say
pages.t: Say that Stormshield holds these European certifications. Do not promise which exact model covers which label: ask a Stormshield contact for the certificate scope. Also notable: IEC 62443-4-1 for secure product development.
g: Standard family for industrial cyber security.

quiz.q: What does a certification show?
quiz.w: Certification means independent testing.

quiz.q: Which French body gives Standard qualification?
quiz.w: ANSSI is the French cyber security agency.

quiz.q: A defence customer asks for NATO RESTRICTED. What do you do?
o: Confirm the label exists and check exact scope with Stormshield
quiz.w: The label exists, but model scope must be confirmed.

quiz.q: What is RESTRICTED?
o: A low classification for sensitive information
quiz.w: It is a lower classification level for sensitive information.

pages.t: Stormshield sells security packs, ongoing maintenance packages that include technical support, patches and updates. Security protection needs to stay current, so renewals matter for resellers.
g: A recurring fee for ongoing service.
Extending a subscription when it expires.

pages.t: Essential covers unified protection: segmentation, secure communications, SD-WAN, intrusion prevention and ZTNA. Premium adds advanced antimalware, AI sandboxing (Breach Fighter) and cloud-based web address filtering for demanding customers.
g: Smart routing across several internet links.
Zero Trust Network Access: no one is trusted by default.
A safe test area where suspicious files are run.

pages.t: Industrial and Industrial Plus packs exist for industrial sites. Maintenance covers support, updates and hardware exchange of a failed unit. Extra services can be added à la carte. Check current pack details with Stormshield.
g: Chosen individually, on top of the base.

quiz.q: What does a security pack mainly provide?
quiz.w: Packs include support, patches and updates.

quiz.q: Which pack adds sandboxing and advanced antimalware?
quiz.w: Premium adds Breach Fighter sandboxing and advanced antimalware.

quiz.q: A customer wants basic unified protection. Which pack?
quiz.w: Essential covers segmentation, IPS, ZTNA and so on.

quiz.q: Why do renewals matter?
quiz.w: Packs keep protection updated and supported.

src.l: Forum thread comparing Fortinet, Sophos, Stormshield

pages.t: In firewalls a customer may compare with international brands such as Fortinet or Sophos. Stormshield's own pitch is European origin, certification and fit, not being the biggest.
g: Another vendor selling a similar product.

pages.t: Stormshield is European, owned by Airbus, with EU and NATO RESTRICTED labels and ANSSI qualification. SNS suits both IT and OT environments, and Stormshield adds endpoint and data products from the same vendor.

Do not claim Stormshield beats everyone on speed. Comparison sheets exist but change often. Lead with trust, European control and certification, then check the specific model with a Stormshield contact.
g: How much traffic a device can handle.

quiz.q: What is Stormshield's best angle against big international brands?
quiz.w: Stormshield's own pitch is European origin, certifications and fit. Avoid blanket speed claims.

quiz.q: Which is true about SNS firewalls?
o: Suited to both IT and OT environments
quiz.w: Stormshield says SNS firewalls are equally suited to IT and OT environments.

quiz.q: A customer asks if Stormshield is faster than a rival. Best reply?
o: Lead with trust and certification, check model data with Stormshield
quiz.w: Do not over-claim performance.

quiz.q: Which of these is a firewall brand a customer might compare with Stormshield?
quiz.w: Fortinet is a large international firewall vendor. Shelly and Shokz sell other kinds of products.

pages.t: Small office: an SN-S (or XS) firewall. Factory: an SNi industrial firewall in the cabinet, plus SNS at the IT edge. Cloud workloads: EVA. Match the product to where it physically sits.
g: The border between a network and the internet.

pages.t: A public body or defence customer cares about certification. Offer SNS with the EU and NATO RESTRICTED story, SES for endpoints, SDS for files, and for vehicles the SNxr1200. Always confirm certificate scope.
g: Fitted inside a vehicle, ship or aircraft.

pages.t: Retail chain with many shops: small SNS boxes plus SMC. Customer wanting visibility: add SLS or XDR. Laptop worries: SES. Sensitive files: SDS. Layers combine, they do not replace each other.

quiz.q: Small office, 20 staff, one site. Best fit?
quiz.w: SN-S fits small businesses.

quiz.q: A bottling plant wants protection in its control cabinets. Best fit?
quiz.w: SNi is the industrial range for cabinets.

quiz.q: A ministry needs a firewall plus sensitive file encryption. Best combo?
o: SNS plus SDS, confirming certificate scope
quiz.w: SNS and SDS match network and data needs with certification.

quiz.q: Which product fits a military vehicle?
quiz.w: The SNxr1200 is the ruggedized model for vehicles.

pages.t: 'We already use another brand.' Suggest a second layer or a certification-driven project. 'Why European?' Data control and certified products. 'Is it only for governments?' No: small models fit small businesses too.
g: A reason the customer gives for not buying.

pages.t: Ask: How many sites? Is there factory or OT equipment? Is anything in the cloud? Do you handle regulated or classified data? Who manages security today? Answers point to the right product.
g: Subject to legal rules about how data is handled.

pages.t: Allnet is a distributor selling to resellers. Do not quote exact specs from memory. Say what the product is for, check models and certificate scope, and bring in the Stormshield team for the details.
g: Sells vendor products to resellers, not to end customers.

quiz.q: A customer says: 'We use another brand.' Good reply?
quiz.w: Find a fit rather than force a switch.

quiz.q: Which question points to the SNi line?
quiz.w: Factory or OT equipment points to SNi.

quiz.q: Which question helps decide on EVA?
o: Is anything running in the cloud?
quiz.w: Cloud workloads point to EVA.

quiz.q: Who does Allnet normally sell to?
quiz.w: Allnet is a distributor selling to resellers.

about: European cybersecurity vendor, owned by Airbus. Best known for network firewalls, and also makes endpoint and data protection.
Sells to defence, public administration, healthcare, transport and critical infrastructure such as water and electric utilities, where product origin and certification matter.
Different from many firewall vendors because it is European, covers both office (IT) and industrial (OT) networks, and carries European security certifications.
